title: Towards Adaptive Neighborhood for Advancing Temporal Interaction Graph Modeling

problem.claim: Temporal Graph Networks model temporal interaction graphs by encoding neighborhoods around target nodes.

gap.claim: Existing Temporal Graph Networks rely on fixed, hand-crafted neighborhood-encoding rules and do not adapt to personalization and temporal evolution across timestamps.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces SEAN, a plug-and-play adaptive neighborhood encoding model for integration with existing Temporal Graph Networks.
SEAN decomposes adaptive neighborhood encoding into representative neighbor selection and temporal-aware neighborhood information aggregation.
The method includes a Representative Neighbor Selector for identifying important neighbors and a Temporal-aware Aggregator for selecting aggregation routes and decaying outdated information.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report integrating SEAN into three representative Temporal Graph Networks and evaluating it on four public datasets and one financial benchmark dataset introduced in the paper.
The authors report consistent performance improvements across all evaluated models, SOTA performance, and exceptional robustness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Temporal Graph Networks perform well for temporal interaction graph modeling by encoding target-node neighborhoods.
Existing methods use fixed hand-crafted neighborhood rules that do not accommodate personalization and temporal evolution.
The paper proposes SEAN, an adaptive neighborhood encoding mechanism with representative neighbor selection and temporal-aware aggregation.
SEAN is integrated into three representative Temporal Graph Networks and evaluated across five datasets or benchmarks.
The authors report improvements across all models, SOTA performance, and exceptional robustness.

source_observation.claim: The method separates adaptive neighborhood encoding into neighbor selection and temporal-aware aggregation.

interpretation.claim: Separating relevance selection from information aggregation can expose distinct mechanisms for personalization and temporal adaptation.

application.claim: For temporal graph systems, consider independently modeling which neighbors matter and how their information should be aggregated over time.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition is beneficial outside the evaluated Temporal Graph Network integrations or datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative performance values or statistical details.
The names and characteristics of the evaluated datasets and benchmarks are not specified.
The abstract does not describe implementation details, computational costs, or ablation results.
